entries.title: The world server no longer crashes with many units close together
entries.body: A line-of-sight check could write past the end of its work list and end the server process without a crash report (Windows error 0xC0000409). It now stops safely at the limit.

entries.title: Experimental Linux server build
entries.body: A Linux build of the server, compiled in Docker on Ubuntu 26.04, is published as an unsigned package for testing. The Manager cannot install it yet.

entries.title: SquidBots builds follow the latest stable module release
entries.body: Nightly builds select the latest stable release tag and pin its exact commit. Bundled release identifiers and settings metadata are supplied to the Manager.

entries.title: Interrupted SquidBots database imports require recovery before restarting
entries.body: Base imports record a pending marker before SQL starts and clear it only after SQL and history recording succeed. A later start detects unfinished imports and requests recovery instead of accepting partially filled tables as complete.

entries.title: SquidBots preserves imported bot databases and skips SQL when disabled
entries.body: Imported installer and update histories prevent SQL replay. Each base file preserves complete existing tables, creates entirely missing tables, and stops on partial structure. Existing bot data without history requires repair. Disabled SquidBots skips SQL.

entries.title: Disabled SquidBots no longer require their database to start the server
entries.body: The server skips registering SquidBots when their master switch is off. Enabling or disabling the module takes effect after a world-server restart; upstream module sources remain unchanged.

entries.title: Large SQUID database imports no longer use the short query timeout
entries.body: Initial imports larger than one megabyte receive up to fifteen minutes to finish. Normal database queries keep their existing deadline, and interrupted imports remain blocked until recovered.

entries.title: First SQUID startup has time to create its initial bot pool
entries.body: The launcher waits longer for the world when SQUID is enabled. Slow initial bot creation no longer uses the three-minute readiness limit intended for ordinary restarts.

entries.title: The Auction House Bot creates its own character when enabled
Imported SquidBots servers warn before replacing their original binary
entries.body: Imports explain that the original launcher and updater check the server binary hash. Updating that binary requires an explicit choice to keep or replace it.

entries.title: Install a server from a package on Linux, running in Docker (experimental)
entries.body: Experimental. The Manager creates the database, imports the packaged baseline and starts the server in Docker containers. It needs a Linux server package and your own game data folder.

entries.title: SquidBots settings follow the options shipped by the module
entries.body: New settings use the module's descriptions, groups, defaults and value limits while retaining existing translations. Unknown formats or invalid fields use built-in controls so the settings page remains available.

entries.title: SquidBots shows its bundled release and includes it in problem reports
entries.body: The Bots and Modules pages and problem reports include the release identifiers. Imported repacks use their recorded bot revision; empty tags are hidden. The settings file's source commit is not presented as the build revision.

entries.title: The NPC Enchanter card explains how to place and remove the NPC
entries.body: The card now shows the two commands: `.npc add 601015` where you stand, and `.npc delete` on the targeted NPC.

entries.title: One button collects all diagnostics, including crashes and Windows crash records
entries.body: Report a problem collects logs, crash reports and small dumps, Windows crash records, update journals and the running server programs in one file, then shows its folder. Crashes without a server crash report are no longer missing.

entries.title: Problem reports go to the right project
entries.body: Choose what the problem is about: Manager and other modules, CoA Companions, or SQUID Playerbots. The report opens in that project's GitHub page with the versions filled in. The bot system that is switched on is preselected.

entries.title: The Auction House Bot card no longer asks for a character GUID
entries.body: Turning the module and the seller on is enough: a server build with the automatic auction character creates its own account and character. The GUID field moved to the advanced settings. The buyer option hint no longer says it spends the auction character's gold.

entries.title: Server updates accept verified published migration variants without rerunning them
entries.body: Signed updates can recognise known published checksums without changing your migration history. Interrupted or failed SQL still requires recovery before retrying.

entries.title: Server updates replace older launchers adapted by the Manager for Wildcard
entries.body: Updates recognize the Manager’s own realm and import adjustments even when older metadata still records the original launcher. New server binaries receive their matching launcher; genuine custom edits still require your decision.

entries.title: Choose and remember the local network address friends use to connect
entries.body: Select an adapter or custom IPv4 address when sharing on LAN. Your choice survives restarts and mode changes; unavailable addresses show a warning instead of silently switching adapters.

entries.title: Older server packages cannot replace a newer installation
entries.body: Update checks stop offering stale packages after an update. To undo an update, use its recovery point instead of applying an older server package.

entries.title: Checking again no longer offers an already installed launcher update
entries.body: The Manager recognizes its own launcher integration while still detecting user edits and changes in newer signed packages.

entries.title: Large SQUID database imports have more time to finish on first startup
entries.body: The Manager allows up to 45 minutes when SQUID Playerbots is enabled, covering its initial database import and bot creation. Ordinary server startup and shutdown keep their existing deadlines.

entries.title: Update history conflicts are detected before server files change
entries.body: Damaged update records block changes and remain visible. Recovery checks saved copies before restoring, and unfinished updates protect backups from deletion and cleanup.

entries.title: Pending database updates remain visible when the server version matches
entries.body: SQL files are checked before replacing server files. Update and recovery attempts refresh their saved status, including errors. Backup deletion cannot race with an update.

entries.title: Diagnostic files with database checks stay readable after secrets are removed
entries.body: Removing a line that mentioned a secret could break the JSON files in a diagnostic package. Secret values are now replaced instead, so the files stay valid.

entries.title: Forming a party with real players no longer crashes the server when CoABotUI is enabled
entries.body: Invalid or stale bot requests are safely rejected, including when bots are disabled.

entries.title: Small groups can enter Dungeon Finder without waiting for five players
entries.body: With group scaling enabled, parties of one to five players can enter together. Server owners can retain standard matchmaking through configuration.

entries.title: Download and update the game client without installing a server
entries.body: Choose to host a server or connect to someone else's. Players joining a friend can download, update and launch the client, save the host's address and use the Manager without installing a local server.

entries.title: Start your installed server or client without downloading an available update
entries.body: Choose to update later and keep playing with your installed version. Interrupted server updates still require recovery before startup.

entries.title: Server updates no longer fail to start with the bundled Python runtime
entries.body: The launcher and its supervisor can load their integration scripts with the repack's isolated Python runtime. This fixes startup failures after an update.

entries.title: Server releases reject versions older than the current stable package
entries.body: Release builds check the stable package version before publishing and require a Manager with the database update safeguards. Manual releases can specify an explicit version when the build date differs from the release date.

entries.title: Grouped bots leave corpse loot to players by default
entries.body: Bots in parties and raids no longer automatically open corpses or take items and money. Server owners can enable the previous behavior in configuration. Solo looting and Need/Greed rolls are unchanged.

entries.title: Adjust dungeon and raid enemy damage from 25% to 200%
entries.body: Choose an enemy damage multiplier on top of group scaling and solo assistance. The default preserves the existing balance. Reload the configuration to apply it without restarting.

entries.title: Open-world life steal can be enabled with a configurable healing percentage
entries.body: Enable passive healing from damage dealt to open-world creatures and choose a percentage from 0 to 100. Players, pets and instances are excluded.

entries.title: Auction bot filters listings using CoA item sources
entries.body: Auction listings use loot, vendor and profession items by default. A master switch and smaller default auction targets make setup easier.

entries.title: Configure partial dungeon parties and open-world life steal in module settings
entries.body: Choose whether Dungeon Finder enters with the current party and enable open-world life steal with a healing percentage from 0 to 100. Available on server builds that support these options.

entries.title: Finish a server update that was blocked by a startup failure
entries.body: The Manager repairs the launcher import path and lets you retry startup for an already applied update. Successful validation finishes the update without replaying SQL or restoring old databases. Failure details are preserved and rollback remains available.

entries.title: Updates restore missing Wildcard character tables without resetting existing data
entries.body: A new corrective update creates only missing Wildcard card and specialization-cache tables. Existing tables and their data are preserved. Release builds now apply SQL on a disposable database before publishing its expected schema.

entries.title: Choose which item types the auction bot sells
entries.body: Switch 15 item categories on or off and adjust listing frequency by quality. Labels and descriptions are translated into all six languages. Changes affect new listings; existing auctions remain.

entries.title: Configure SQUID Playerbots and prevent conflicting bot systems
entries.body: The Bots tab shows translated settings for the active bot system. Bot module cards keep enable switches without duplicate settings. Enable one bot system at a time; the Manager checks manual config changes before starting the server. Recovery points also include the SQUID database when installed.

entries.title: Module settings now offer translated controls and an enemy damage slider
entries.body: Configure scaling, auctions and enchantments with translated controls. Module switches no longer appear twice. Modules without settings hide their settings button; short lists need no search. New server builds support dungeon and raid damage from 25% to 200%.

entries.title: Failed server updates restore databases and files together
entries.body: Updates save a full backup and recover databases and files together. Interrupted SQL is not replayed. Checks cover Wildcard tables and every supported race/class pair, including existing characters. Unfinished updates block startup until recovered.

entries.title: Server packages must include a complete database schema check
entries.body: Release tools generate the expected database structure on an isolated copy of the signed base, verify all archive files and refuse packages without the schema check. Corrective SQL can restore missing Wildcard tables without replaying old updates.

entries.title: Open remote-console connections no longer prevent server shutdown
entries.body: The shutdown fix is merged in the server source. A server package containing it is required; updating the Manager alone does not update the server binaries.

entries.title: Check database structure and repair server files with a safety backup
entries.body: Settings can check both realm databases and restore official files plus pending SQL. Installation and updates check character-save columns. Clean packages no longer keep old character migration records when rebuilding their database.

entries.title: Start CoA and Wildcard together from Settings
entries.body: Both worlds can run on separate ports with their own characters, settings and logs, sharing accounts. Stop saves both worlds before shutting down the shared database.

entries.title: Server multipliers now accept decimals typed with a dot or comma
entries.body: Talent settings now explain that the multiplier does not affect CoA talents. The rested experience setting now correctly describes bonus accumulation.

entries.title: Play launches only the game client without starting your local server
entries.body: Use the left button to start the server and PLAY to launch the client with your selected realmlist, including connections to other servers.

entries.title: Companions follow safer navigation paths
entries.body: Companion movement uses validated paths and geometry checks, reducing unsafe movement and keeping recovery behavior consistent when a route fails.

entries.title: Dungeon Finder respects scaled realm levels across enabled expansions
entries.body: Dungeon access checks use the realm progression ranges, and Dungeon Finder defaults to the server expansion. Enabled Classic, Burning Crusade and Wrath content remains visible at a reduced level cap.

entries.title: Companions follow and recover movement more consistently
entries.body: Updated movement handling coordinates following, mounting and route recovery so interrupted actions do not take over a newer movement request.

entries.title: Companions fly from the opening of Burning Crusade content
entries.body: Companions can mount for flight from the realm’s Burning Crusade unlock level instead of a fixed level 60, and switch from ground mounts when the leader flies.

entries.title: Companions avoid helmets and shoulders with missing models
entries.body: Equipment repair rejects display models missing from the audited client, preventing broken helmet and shoulder visuals.

entries.title: Companion equipment repair continues with full bags
entries.body: When a companion has full bags, equipment replaced by the gear filter is preserved in its mailbox. The gradual repair queue no longer stalls because old items cannot fit in the inventory.

entries.title: All dungeon difficulties and combat gear variants follow realm progression
entries.body: Classic, BC and Wrath normal, heroic and mythic queues support bot-fill or current-party entry. Reference loot and combat gear variants, including Bloodforged, scale requirements and stats while retaining difficulty progression. Forge of Souls quests use their actual expansion.

entries.title: Custom progression at level 80 now scales item requirements and rewards consistently
entries.body: Custom era boundaries now apply to item budgets, quest XP, dungeon access and group finder rewards even when the maximum player level is 80.

entries.title: Downscaled dungeon creatures keep their loot rewards
entries.body: The damage needed to earn loot now follows a creature's scaled health, including encounter health changes. Player participation is still required.

entries.title: Dungeon Finder shows all enabled expansions at a reduced level cap
entries.body: Updated client addon support displays the server's effective dungeon level ranges. Earlier expansions stay available through the level cap; quest and equipment requirements still apply.

entries.title: Items now scale correctly on servers with a reduced level cap
entries.body: Equipment stats, item levels and required levels are adjusted after item data loads. Dungeon item-level requirements follow the same scaling.

entries.title: Scaled encounters retain normal boss loot
entries.body: Dungeon and raid encounters preserve their normal loot when scaled for smaller groups. Equipment is no longer randomly discarded in favor of currency.

entries.title: Remote console shutdown no longer blocks server management
entries.body: Graceful shutdown through the remote console releases pending console requests so the manager can stop the worldserver and switch realms reliably.

entries.title: Bots get level-appropriate gear without holiday, event or vanity items
entries.body: Equipment checks required level, item level and PvE/PvP Power. Use .fixbotgear to repair existing bots gradually. Suitable gear stays; replaced items remain in bags or are mailed when bags are full. The repair queue survives server restarts.

entries.title: Existing bots follow a lowered server level cap
entries.body: Bots above the cap are lowered when they log in. Online bots are handled gradually outside combat, with experience reset and replacement gear queued.

entries.title: Destroyed instances release their saved scaling state
entries.body: Encounter snapshots and group scaling settings are cleared when a map is destroyed, preventing stale state from reaching a later instance that reuses its ID.

entries.title: Invalid progression settings stop scaling before items are changed
entries.body: If the progression layout fails validation, scaling initialization stops before item templates are modified or combat hooks are enabled.

entries.title: Disabling Content Scaling now stops item and group finder changes
entries.body: After restarting the worldserver, disabled scaling preserves original items and group finder rules. Creature and quest levels, combat, rewards and encounter mechanics also retain their original behavior.

entries.title: Explicit scaling overrides now take priority over generated content profiles
entries.body: Map overrides apply to creatures on every map, area overrides take priority for quests, and item era overrides retain each item's safety protections.

entries.title: The game client follows the realm selected in the Manager
entries.body: Switching realms updates the closed client's saved realm automatically. Play checks it again before launch, preventing login attempts to the previous realm. If the client is running, the update waits until the next launch.

entries.title: Experimental Linux startup and Docker server controls
entries.body: The Manager can start on Linux and control manually prepared Docker servers. One-click installation, updates, backups and Wine or Proton client launch are not available yet.

entries.title: Simplified Chinese is available in the Manager
entries.body: The interface and server and bot settings are now available in Simplified Chinese. Choose Simplified Chinese in the language selector.

entries.title: Configuration snapshots no longer overwrite each other
entries.body: Snapshots created close together keep separate copies, so restoring a configuration reliably restores the selected snapshot.

entries.title: Problem reports open in the default browser
entries.body: GitHub reports open in the default browser instead of Windows Explorer. Long reports use the clipboard fallback.

entries.title: Stock tab shows each item's limit
entries.body: A gold limit line appears under the item and updates as soon as you set it.

entries.title: A missing config option is reported once, not on every world tick
entries.body: Servers lacking some module config files logged two lines per tick and filled the logs.

entries.title: Switch between CoA and Wildcard while keeping separate characters and module settings
entries.body: Run one world at a time with shared accounts. Wildcard keeps its own progress; CoA companions are unavailable there, and other modules show experimental compatibility. Backups and server updates cover both realms.

entries.title: Updating the game client shows a progress bar on its button
entries.body: No window covers the app while the client updates.

entries.title: Imported servers get the module config files they lack
entries.body: They are created at start and after an update; existing files are never changed.

entries.title: Modules marked Soon stay greyed out
The Bots page is hidden when the module is not on the server
Dungeons and raids scale to your group size, with solo modes
entries.body: Content Scaling is on by default. Switch it off on the Manager's Modules page to keep stock difficulty.

entries.title: TBC and WotLK content packs
entries.body: Outland and Northrend dungeons and raids, scaled to your level range.

entries.title: Boss health scaling reads the real raid difficulty table
entries.body: Fixes a start-up stop on servers built from the shipped SQL.

entries.title: NPC Enchanter may say an empty line on servers without its config file
entries.body: Copy npc_enchanter.conf.dist to npc_enchanter.conf, or let the Manager create it.

entries.title: Bots no longer take Realm First achievements
entries.body: Set Achievement.RealmFirstBlockBots = 0 to allow it again.

entries.title: Starter pack bots get 22-slot bags
Trade with your bots
entries.body: Open a trade window and hand a bot items directly, no more mailing them.

entries.title: Dungeon fill picks bots by role more reliably
NPC Enchanter in Orgrimmar and Stormwind
entries.body: Beauregard Boneglitter stands next to the War Games organizer.

entries.title: Browse tab lists every online bot
entries.body: Filter by role, class, level, guildmates or name and invite to your group or guild. It replaces the /who workaround, which stays capped at 49 names.

entries.title: Collect gold and Stock tabs for the bot economy
Invite one bot by role
entries.body: Choose tank, healer or damage and a free bot of your faction joins your group.

entries.title: Bot economy, experimental and off by default
entries.body: Gold orders, stock limits, selling surplus on the auction house, a guild share and level-appropriate food. Enable with CoaBots.Economy.Enable = 1; it starts in dry-run mode.

entries.title: Master switch for the companion bots
entries.body: CoaBots.Enable = 0 stops all bot spawning. The Manager's Modules page switches it.

entries.title: A huge .botcmd spawnrandom no longer floods the server
entries.body: The count is clamped and bots spawn in small batches.

entries.title: Auction House Bot is built in but inactive until configured
Optional fee for the NPC Enchanter
entries.body: Set Enchanter.CostCopper in copper; 0 keeps the enchantments free.

entries.title: Collections tab with transmog, vanity, riding and companion switches
Delete an account from the Players page
entries.body: You type the account name to confirm; online and system accounts are refused.

entries.title: Modules page with cards, status badges and per-module settings
entries.body: Switch the companion bots and NPC Enchanter on and off; a module's settings open under its card.

entries.title: Importing a server suggests the right folder when you pick the wrong one
Report a problem collects more and ignores repeated config warnings
Server settings in one panel with search, tabs and a single Save bar
Companion bots are recognised from their default config file
The update check says you are up to date instead of offering the same version
